annotations.text:
Vamp Assistant — paper, ink, one orange

A second direction, drawn from scratch: an ivory ground instead of grey, a serif to name things and a sans to operate them, hairlines instead of boxes, and a single accent spent once per screen. Glass appears only where something genuinely floats — the bar, a sheet, a popover.

Every pair is contrast-checked: ink 16.4:1 on paper, the accent 4.5:1 and 4.9:1 under white; at night 16.2:1 and 8.0:1.
Sessions: the Mac's four actions between two rules, then the list. No cards, no fills, no chrome below.
The prompt is the only thing in a container; the answer is on the page. Tool steps hang off a single rule. The one orange on screen is the send button and the caret.
The question is set in the serif, the four settings are cells between rules, and the first message is typed in the same composer as every message after it.
The Mac is the same system at desk scale: a sidebar of hairline rows, one reading column, the plan as a list, the approval as an outline, and the composer with ⌘↩ where the phone shows a send button.
